propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang times out after 300s and raises SnapshotFetchError, which is caught as a generic exception and converted to a fail-closed LLM-Review -1 vote.
The spurious -1 vote is durable because reconcile.py's backfill pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote and skips any change that already has a vote, permanently suppressing retry.
The adapter's blanket exception handler cannot distinguish retryable infrastructure faults (network stall, timeout, connection error) from genuine review conclusions, so both paths vote fail-closed.
A change that receives a spurious -1 from a transient fetch stall is removed from backfill's safety net and wedged until manual re-trigger.

The system already implements correct no-vote behavior for hung reviews one layer up (app.py, reconcile.py), so the fix is to make the adapter and voter return ABSTAIN and emit no vote when encountering retryable infrastructure exceptions.

Acceptance requires that retryable exceptions (SnapshotFetchError, TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) result in no vote and no dedup row, while genuine review conclusions and non-retryable exceptions still vote fail-closed.
